blocks.text: Have you ever wondered why your bank statement shows a different balance than your cash book? Let's explore the reasons and how to reconcile them.

blocks.markdown: Bank reconciliation is a crucial process in accounting that helps ensure the accuracy of a company's financial records. It involves comparing the cash book balance with the bank statement balance and identifying any discrepancies.

blocks.title: Definition of Bank Reconciliation
blocks.text: Bank reconciliation is the process of matching and comparing figures from the accounting records against those presented on a bank statement.

blocks.markdown: There are several reasons why the cash book balance might differ from the bank statement balance. These include outstanding cheques, deposits in transit, bank charges, direct credits, and errors in recording transactions.

blocks.title: Updating the Cash Book
blocks.prompt: Let's update the cash book for bank charges and direct credits.

steps.text: Start with the cash book balance: ₦10,000.

blocks.answer: The updated cash book balance is ₦10,500.

blocks.markdown: Once the cash book is updated, the next step is to prepare the bank reconciliation statement. This statement will list all the items causing the discrepancies, such as outstanding cheques and deposits in transit.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Always ensure that all bank charges and direct credits are recorded in the cash book before preparing a bank reconciliation statement.

points: Bank reconciliation helps identify discrepancies between the cash book and bank statement.
Common causes of differences include bank charges, outstanding cheques, and deposits in transit.
